chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The woman inherits from the wergild (blood money) of her husband, and he inherits from her wergild, so long as one of the two has not killed his partner.

key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money paid for homicide or injury

ai.seo_question: Does a husband and wife inherit each other's blood money if one kills the other?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the general prohibition of 'ghulul' (exclusion due to major sin) does not apply to spousal inheritance of blood money, provided the killer is not the spouse themselves. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the killer's exclusion is specific to the direct victim, allowing the surviving spouse to inherit the deceased's diyah from the killer, a nuance distinct from some Sunni interpretations regarding the killer's share. This ruling underscores the principle that marital bonds remain valid for inheritance purposes even in cases of homicide, unless the killer is the direct heir.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The woman would inherit from the wergild of her husband, and he would inherit from her wergild, so long as one of the two has not killed his partner’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following: “Abu Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A woman inherits from the wergild of her husband and her husband inherits from the wergild of his wife as long as one of them does not kill the other partner.’”
